name: CODEFIX-75
SONAR-23098
text:
Import project dependencies
CONTEXT FOSSA  customers can see FOSSA's results in SonarQube. Developers are empowered to fix more issues that make the overall software less hardened because FOSSA issues are visible as part of their daily workflow. WHAT This will be an  enterprise+ feature Introduce the concept of project dependencies.  Allow the scanner to provide the list of project dependencies and dependency graphs for each analysis.  Update the Fossa Sensor to feed those values. A new  Dependencies  tab appears on projects. When a Fossa report is scanned, dependencies are persisted and shown in this tab with the following information: Total number of dependencies Dependencies names Dependencies versions Transitive  or  Direct  tag: There will be a limitation for this sprint, where we show  Transitive  everywhere, the correct info will be computed in a later Sprint. A search input allows filtering dependencies by key (exact match) and long name (partial match). A new V2 endpoint  /api/v2/analysis/dependencies  is available for the Search.

text:
Quality profiles support customization of impact severities
CONTEXT See  . WHAT The application will provide the ability to change the impact severity on a rule activated in a quality profile The following endpoints will be updated  qualityprofiles/activate_rule add a new parameter ‘impacts’. It contains a semi-colon separated list of impacts with their severity: reliability=BLOCKER;security=HIGH rules/search the response will change to add the impact defined on the active rules  "impacts": [                 {                     "softwareQuality": "RELIABILITY",                     "severity": "MEDIUM"                 },                 {                     "softwareQuality": "MAINTAINABILITY",                     "severity": "MEDIUM"                 }             ] qualityprofiles/compare The response will change : The ‘modified’ section contains a list of modified Quality Profiles. The ‘impacts’ field needs to be moved in the ‘right’ and ‘left’ fields instead of being at the ‘Quality Profile’ level. Only the differing impacts will be returned in ‘left’ and ‘right’ fields

name: SONAR-23427
text:
Stop relying on Qualifiers, Scopes and ResourceType from the plugin API
CONTEXT The concept of component qualifier and scope is something mostly internal to the platform. It is only exposed in a few web APIs, and it should not be part of the plugin API. We are adding a new type of component for dependencies, and we don’t want to expose that in the plugin API. WHAT Remove any dependency on  org.sonar.api.resources.Qualifiers  ,  org.sonar.api.resources.Scopes  ,  org.sonar.api.resources.ResourceType  ,  org.sonar.api.resources.ResourceTypes

name: SONAR-23430
text:
Improve api/system/liveness action to not pollute the logs
CONTEXT When the SonarQube is (re)starting the calls to  api/system/liveness  might for a brief period of time return HTTP 500. At the same time they report error log. Logging an exception for this endpoint is not the best implementation as the node being alive or not are the very things that this endpoint is expected to verify. WHAT Improve the endpoint in a way that it doesn’t throw exception when the node is not alive.

name: SONAR-23466
text:
Rules indexing is not happening consistently
CONTEXT In the context of  , we have added 2 built-in rules. Built-in rules are rules that are not coming from plugins. As a consequence, the strategy to detect if a rule has been updated needed to be refactored. WHAT The RuleRegistrant class goal is to register rule changes at startup, both for technical purposes (DB / ES changes), but also for functional needs (like quality profile changelog). There is also a mechanism to detect that the Elast Search index is corrupted or missing, and in this case all rules should be indexed again. Something has been broken by   and now, when the data/es folder is deleted, it is re-created but the rule index is empty. Steps to reproduce: start a fresh SQ 10.7, login and navigate to the rules section. It should contain many rules + facets. stop the server delete the data/es folder restart the server. The rules section is now empty. This is affecting mainly users running SonarQube in a container, because the default approach is to not persist ES indexes, so every restart of the container is like starting the server with a clean data/es folder. WORKAROUND CAUTION: this will trigger a full Elastic Search indexing, and this may take some time on big instances. Stop the SonarQube server Delete the  data/es  folder in the SonarQube installation directory Connect to the SonarQube database, and execute the SQL query:  UPDATE PLUGINS SET FILE_HASH = ''  to emulate a change on all plugins Start the server FIX I am suggesting to take a safe approach and revert all changes made to rule registration in   . The RuleRegistrant class is very complex, so trying another fix might create other unexpected problems. The only downside of this revert is that any change to the 2 built-in SCA rules definition won’t be indexed until another plugin is changed in the instance. We can live with that constraint in the meantime.
